why: A perfect set is a chain v, v^2, v^4, ... with every value present. Put the values in a hash set, start only at values whose square root is not present, and walk v -> v*v while it exists; this is the longest-consecutive-sequence trick with squaring instead of +1, and chains are at most 5 long under 10^6.
hints: Once the smallest bag of a perfect set is fixed, the whole set is forced. What is it?
From any start v the chain is v, v^2, v^4, ... while present. Use a hash set for O(1) lookups and only start from values whose integer square root is not in the set.
For each chain start, count steps while cur*cur is in the set; keep the max; return -1 if it is below 2. Roughly O(n) since a chain has at most 5 values below 10^6.
pitfalls: A single bag is not a perfect set; return -1 when no chain reaches length 2.
Compute integer square roots exactly (math.isqrt), floating sqrt can be off by one.
cur*cur can grow huge; stop as soon as it exceeds the maximum value.
